rows.claim: No count or liveness claim is filed without re-running the bytes that produce it; the seed carries the estate's own fossil (39-green was 1305/34/9) as the cost of skipping this once.
rows.quote: Never trust a hand-written count, including your own from an earlier session.
rows.steal: Before filing any battery row, re-run the count command myself and paste raw output to the archive file; landing: gala w2 lanes check files.
rows.falsifier: A filed count whose command cannot be re-run to reproduce it (or whose archive file lacks the raw output) voids the row.

rows.claim: The five build-discipline laws transfer because they ship as runnable mechanics (ratchet command, freshness command) with a registered-debt escape, not as advice; the only forbidden direction is backward.
rows.quote:
A ban fails the day it meets reality and gets loosened. A ratchet starts where the
estate actually is: existing debt is registered BY NAME (who accepted it, so debt has
an owner), and the only forbidden direction is backward.
rows.steal: Convert one standing review-law reminder into a check command with a baseline file (accept debt by name, block new debt); landing: tools/ violation-style check + configs baseline json.
rows.falsifier: Introduce one new violation past the baseline: if the check exits 0, the ratchet claim is false; if the baseline itself can be loosened without a named owner, the escape is not honest.

rows.claim: No seed version ships on builder say-so: tools/cold_boot_test.py copies the package to a stripped temp dir and runs FIRST_BOOT steps 0-7 with no estate environment; readable failure is a pass, traceback is a fail.
rows.quote:
Copies seed/ to a fresh temp dir, then runs FIRST_BOOT steps 0-7 verbatim with no
estate environment.
rows.steal: Run the cold-boot harness as the last gate before every zip/export (test-then-strip-then-ship order); landing: seed build-book pre-zip step.
rows.falsifier: A cook that passes verify_seal but exits nonzero or emits a Traceback/ModuleNotFoundError mark under cold_boot_test proves the seal alone is not a ship bar (this is exactly how V1 died: 2 of 7 cold-boot steps).

rows.claim: A 59-row sha256 manifest plus a 15-line verifier makes the whole method pack tamper-evident and portable: 59/59 verified on the live tree and 59/59 re-verified by stock sha256sum inside the extracted zip, with only MANIFEST.sha256 itself unsealed.
rows.quote: check every file in MANIFEST.sha256 against its hash. Exit 0 = intact.
rows.steal: Give every exported artifact bundle a MANIFEST.sha256 + two-line verifier so any receiver can prove the pack intact without trusting the sender; landing: watch/inbox export convention receipt line.
rows.falsifier: Flip one byte in any sealed file: verify_seal must print DRIFT naming that file and exit 1; if it exits 0 the seal is decoration, not a RIB.
